---
title: "Fit a mixed model"
---

Fit test scores on study hours with a random intercept for each school, then read the fixed effects, the variance components, and each school's estimated effect.

The example runs with the phit extension or the plain-PHP polyfill ([Extension or polyfill](../extension-or-polyfill.qmd)). The data are 30 simulated students, five from each of six schools, taken from [`docs/data/schools.csv`](https://github.com/phpstats/phit/blob/main/docs/data/schools.csv). `score` is a test score in points, and `study_hours` is time spent studying, in hours.

## Code

```php
use function Phit\fit_mixed_gaussian;

// One line per school, five students each.
$students = [
    'school' => array_merge(...array_map(
        fn ($s) => array_fill(0, 5, "school-0$s"),
        range(1, 6),
    )),
    'study_hours' => [
        11.58, 2.7, 10.02, 3.71, 4.38,
        4.3, 2.8, 11.5, 1.15, 3.9,
        7.27, 1.24, 6.08, 1.37, 11.43,
        8.82, 11.44, 5.52, 2.04, 4.93,
        3.52, 3.39, 1.15, 8.2, 9.63,
        6.3, 9.93, 2.54, 2.08, 5.78,
    ],
    'score' => [
        78.3, 67.2, 88.2, 68.5, 60.1,
        69.2, 59.1, 92.1, 64.4, 67.1,
        72.9, 55.8, 62.6, 52.6, 83.1,
        63.7, 83.9, 52.8, 51.9, 57.1,
        68.3, 67.6, 60.5, 81.6, 75.2,
        81.5, 89.4, 60.7, 62.5, 68.6,
    ],
];

$fit = fit_mixed_gaussian(
    'score ~ study_hours + (1 | school)',
    $students,
);

foreach ($fit['columns'] as $i => $name) {
    printf(
        "%-12s %7.2f (se %.2f)\n",
        $name,
        $fit['coefficients'][$i],
        $fit['std_errors'][$i],
    );
}

$school = $fit['random'][0];
printf(
    "\nschool SD %.2f, residual SD %.2f\n\n",
    sqrt($school['covariance'][0][0]),
    $fit['sigma'],
);

foreach ($school['group_labels'] as $g => $label) {
    $se = sqrt($school['effects_cond_var'][$g][0][0]);
    printf(
        "%s %+6.2f (se %.2f)\n",
        $label,
        $school['effects'][$g][0],
        $se,
    );
}
```

## Output

```
(Intercept)    53.29 (se 2.70)
study_hours     2.77 (se 0.27)

school SD 4.93, residual SD 5.10

school-01  +0.99 (se 2.07)
school-02  +3.27 (se 2.07)
school-03  -2.54 (se 2.07)
school-04  -7.89 (se 2.07)
school-05  +2.47 (se 2.07)
school-06  +3.69 (se 2.07)
```

## Interpretation

- `(1 | school)` gives each school its own intercept, assumed to come from a normal distribution. The fit uses REML, as `lme4::lmer()` does by default.
- The `study_hours` coefficient is an association within schools. The model gives every school the same slope.
- The school SD describes how school intercepts vary. The residual SD describes how students vary around their school's line.
- With six schools, the school SD is estimated imprecisely.
- `effects` are each school's predicted intercept relative to the average, as R's `ranef()` reports. They are shrunk toward zero, more so for schools with fewer students.
- The conditional standard errors are equal because every school has five students.

**See also:** [Mixed models](../mixed-models.qmd) for the supported structures, the full result, singular fits, and `fit_mixed_logistic()` · [Interactive shrinkage vignette](https://phit.phpstats.org/vignettes/school-shrinkage)
